ashok: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing we move from hard region-penalty buckets to a 'soft affinity score' that lives in the policy engine. Goal: reduce flip-flopping during noisy probe windows and improve tail latency for critical tenants.

maria: Can you sketch the policy surface? e.g. how do scores combine with cost/latency weights? Additive or multiplicative? Any perf impact?

ashok: Sketch: affinity is a normalized float in [0,1]. Policy score = (latency_score * (1 - alpha + alpha * affinity)) + cost_penalty. Where alpha is a tunable importance knob. Multiplicative-ish so affinity strengthens latency signal without fully overriding cost. Runtime perf: one extra float per route, negligible. Need unit tests + sim harness to validate oscillation.

kevin: Ops concerns: if affinity window is too short we'll get churn. Need guardrail: only apply affinity for tenants > 50 qps or when probe stdev < threshold. Also require a "stability" gate (N consecutive probe ticks) before toggling active affinity.

lia: Telemetry thoughts: affinity_histogram, affinity_churn_rate, route_swap_rate_1m/5m, and tail_lat_ms per tenant. Canary plan: header-injected flag + traffic-split. Add dashboards for swap heatmaps.

deploy-bot: New config uploaded: rfc/affinity-probe-v1 (https://redwood.internal/rfcs/affinity-probe-v1) :white_check_mark:

ashok: Fallback semantics: if affinity < 0.2 fallback to region-agnostic baseline model variant. Keep preemptive slotting unchanged. We'll also add a separate "stability_score" that requires X consecutive positive probes to flip affinity on/off.

maria: Cost fairness: what if affinity routes traffic to a more expensive region? Must surface a tenant budget cap and a "cost_override" boolean on the policy DSL. Default behavior: do not increase expected spend beyond tenant budget; affinity may prefer cheaper regions when possible.

kevin: Implementation note: policy engine will publish a candidate route list with normalized scores. Runtime picks top-K, then hedges: primary + optional secondary fanout until response thresholds met. Ensure we don't double-request for low-qps customers — hedge only when latency SLO risk is high.

lia: I'll add sim scenarios: bursty traffic, steady traffic, probe outages. Measure an "oscillation index" and end-to-end tail latency vs cost. Plan: 2-week sim, then 1% canary for 48h, 10% with active monitoring, then ramp.

ashok: Action items: @maria add budget/cost_override fields to DSL + example policies, @kevin spec runtime contract for top-K + hedging, @lia prepare telemetry + sim dashboard. I'll draft follow-up RFC with config examples and sim results template. :thumbsup:

maria: ack — will include migration notes for existing penalty buckets and a default decay policy.

kevin: ack — will push runtime interface PR tomorrow and annotate edge-cases (low qps, degens).

lia: ack — scheduling sims and dashboard widgets now.

ashok: Thanks all — I'll post the RFC link once drafted. If anyone sees a gotcha (especially around preemption or quota accounting) ping here. :eyes:
